slot.brief: Given r(t), differentiate to find the velocity vector and its magnitude at a given time.

stem: A particle moves in a plane with position vector $\vec{r}(t) = (4t^2+t)\hat{i} + (5t^2+2t)\hat{j}$ m, where $t$ is in seconds. Its velocity vector and speed at $t=1$ s are

verdicts.working: Differentiate: \(\vec v=(8t+1)\hat i+(10t+2)\hat j\). At \(t=1\), \(\vec v=9\hat i+12\hat j\) m s\(^{-1}\), with speed \(\sqrt{9^2+12^2}=15\) m s\(^{-1}\).

working:
$\vec{v}=\dfrac{d\vec{r}}{dt}=(8t+1)\hat{i}+(10t+2)\hat{j}$
At $t=1$ s: $\vec{v}=(9\hat{i}+12\hat{j})$ m s$^{-1}$
$|\vec{v}|=\sqrt{9^2+12^2}=15$ m s$^{-1}$

Independent check: Differentiate: \(\vec v=(8t+1)\hat i+(10t+2)\hat j\). At \(t=1\), \(\vec v=9\hat i+12\hat j\) m s\(^{-1}\), with speed \(\sqrt{9^2+12^2}=15\) m s\(^{-1}\).
solution:
Velocity is the time derivative of position:
$$\vec{v}=\frac{d\vec{r}}{dt}=(8t+1)\hat{i}+(10t+2)\hat{j}.$$
At $t=1$ s, $\vec{v}=(9\hat{i}+12\hat{j})$ m s$^{-1}$ and $|\vec{v}|=\sqrt{9^2+12^2}=15$ m s$^{-1}$. Do not add chit-chat.
